title: Compile safety envelope and pin rotation for non-uniform expert topologies
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: When onboarding MoE and other non-uniform expert topologies we see high variance in per-shard compile success, performance regressions due to brittle kernel choices, and occasional OOMs at production shapes. This ticket defines a 'compile safety envelope' (CSE) for each model signature and implements a pin-rotation policy that: 1) publishes a conservative baseline profile into the runtime registry, 2) stages experimental higher-performance profiles behind a canary rotation that is traffic-weighted and telemetry-gated, and 3) provides an automated rollback when SLO regressions or increased error rates are detected.

Goals:
- Reduce probability of a failed or regressing compile after model onboarding by >= 90% compared to current ad-hoc pins.
- Ensure no more than 5% tail latency regression across production workload slices during profile rotation.
- Provide reproducible provenance for every published profile (commit + compile args + kernel fingerprint).

Approach:
- Define CSE: a compact set of compile flags and kernel affinity bounds that must pass a deterministic smoke benchmark for MHA, GQA and MoE variants before being considered publishable. CSEs are conservative (favor success & safety).
- Pin rotation controller: a controller that sequences profiles: baseline -> staged -> canary -> promoted. Each stage advances based on telemetry gates (latency/CER/token-cost) over a sliding window.
- Telemetry instrumentation: add new metrics (profile_success_rate, compile_time_p50/p95, fallback_count, tail_latency_diff, kv-saturation) and attach them to model-version and shard-fingerprint tags.
- Experiment harness: use existing onboarding CI to submit synthetic traces that emulate multi-expert routing and GQA sparsity, validate profiles at different sequence lengths and batch shapes.
- Rollback policy: immediate rollback if profile_success_rate drops below 98% or tail latency increases by > 10% on production traffic for >5 minutes.

Out of scope: per-customer rate limiting for canaries (handled by Dedicated rollout flow), full UI for profile history (Console task).

Artifacts: design doc: https://go.redwood/design/compile-safety-envelope, onboarding spec: https://drive.redwood/model-onboard/moe-cse, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3147, dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood/runtime/profiles/ENG-384729
acceptance_criteria: CSE verifier runs in CI and validates three representative MoE/GQA/MHA samples within 2 hours
Controller can advance a profile from staged -> canary on test cluster and collect gated metrics
Telemetry tags emitted for profile_id, model_version, shard_fingerprint, and route_hash
Automatic rollback triggers in canary when configured thresholds violated (tested via fault injection)
Published profile includes provenance blob (git_sha, compile_flags, kernel_manifest) and is discoverable via registry API
comments: 2026-01-12 Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for ENG-472019. Root cause summary: default aggressive compile flags selected for an MoE variant caused kernel OOM on 80% of shards during high-batch synthetic runs.

2026-01-18 Liam Chen: Drafted CSE schema + initial verifier harness. Pushed prototype verifier to PR 3147. Observed that disabling a single fusion pass reduces OOMs but increases p50 by ~6% on small sequences.
2026-01-22 Diego Alvarez: Telemetry schema reviewed. Added profile_id and shard_fingerprint tags. Suggested collecting nvtx ranges for hot-path attribution.
2026-01-27 QA: Canary job ran with staged profile across 5% synthetic traffic; profile_success_rate=99.1% but tail_latency_diff=+8% on 2048-token long-seq; we flagged for another iteration.
2026-02-01 PM review (Ava Roberts): Approved rollout policy conditional on automated rollback within 3m of threshold breach. Added requirement for runbook and on-call notification mapping.

2026-02-03 Liam Chen: Updated controller to emit canary_state events and to call the rollback webhook. Integration tests added to runtime CI. Next: expand synthetic workload shapes and run cross-arch verification.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: the CSE baseline will likely be downgraded in perf vs. current aggressive pins, but the goal is operational stability during onboarding. Future follow-ups will target automated profile optimization once rotation is stable.
